cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Mum, we signed the lease. Say it's good news before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I know. I still want my mother to be pleased.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you toast both of us? I want to remember you welcoming our home, not just tolerating my address.

mechanism: A directs a celebratory toast while needing a mother genuine welcome for the already-chosen shared home.
confusable: D57 public deference can be merely ceremonial; D76 requires approval from this emotionally important person, not anyone with a glass.
comparison: A mother including Sam in a toast differs from a father preparing tools for a new job.
seedUse: Use D76-b signed lease and partial welcome; make A revise the permitted toast to seek blessing for both partners.
